agent.problem: The stop repeatedly quizzes genealogies and name lists: cards 2, 3, 6-9, 13, 15, 17, 18 and 20 all ask about details inside those stretches. The embedded Ephraim family anecdotes do not permit choice cards either; the rule explicitly treats a short story inside a genealogy as part of the stretch.

rule.text: Papa Dorin sums up the stretch in one story card. A short story inside the stretch, like Nimrod in the list of nations (Genesis 10:8–12), is part of the stretch: it can be the standout detail on that card, but it gets no choice cards. A stretch never gets a stop of its own. Its one card sits in the stop with the moments around it. He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item. He can name a standout detail the text gives if it helps the stretch stick. The baker should know the stretch is there and what it's about, not memorize it. A long stretch never gets a choice card.

agent.problem: Most of the choice cards require luck or outside recall rather than reasoning from the earlier cards. There is no contextual basis for picking the answers on cards 2, 3, 8, 9, 13, 15, 17, 18 or 20. Only cards 6 and 7 provide meaningful reasoning context, so discovery questions dominate the stop instead of remaining a few exceptions.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

human.problem: The whole passage, 1 Chronicles 7:1-8:40, is a genealogy with census counts and town lists, and it contains a few short stories: Ephraim's loss, Sheerah's towns, Beriah and Shema driving out Gath. The long-stretch rule says to sum up a stretch in one story card, says a stretch never gets a choice card or a stop of its own, and says a short story inside a stretch gets no choice cards. Followed literally, this passage could not have a stop at all, and it could not meet the rule that choice cards are equal to or more than story cards. The walkthrough instead uses several summary cards (cards 4, 11, 12 and 14) and 11 choice cards on genealogy details (cards 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 13, 15, 17, 18 and 20).
human.question: When a passage is entirely a long stretch, like a genealogy chapter, how should Prep be built? May it break the stretch into several summary cards and ask choice cards about the standout details and short stories inside it, or should it be handled some other way?

human.question: Can a summary story card for a long stretch go past 2 sentences, as the Genesis 5 example does? If so, what is the limit?

human.question: How should Prep handle a passage that is entirely a long stretch, like a genealogy chapter? May it ask choice cards about standout details, such as the Gath raid, Beriah's name, Sheerah, Joshua and Saul? If so, how many, and does the choice-to-story ratio still apply? Or should such a passage get a reduced or different walkthrough?
